title: Introduce provider compatibility layer and explicit networking module contracts
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Goal: Reduce future terraform provider upgrade friction and decouple networking responsibilities by introducing a lightweight provider compatibility layer and an explicit v2 networking contract for route/table/nat lifecycle. This ticket covers design, module refactor, CI gating, and an automated state-migration plan to move a subset of workspaces to the new modules.

Background: We've experienced multiple incidents and long rollbacks when upgrading AWS/GCP providers because modules implicitly relied on provider behavior and cross-module side effects (implicit route table changes, EIP lifecycle). We also lack a clear surface contract for networking modules which makes refactors risky. The aim is to: (1) establish a provider-compat shim abstraction that allows pinning or polyfilling provider differences during upgrades, (2) publish a canonical networking v2 module interface and migration guide, (3) add CI Terratest smoke coverage and plan-only checks per-workspace, and (4) run a canary migration on two non-critical workspaces before wider rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
- Provider compat layer implemented as a thin wrapper module and documented in CONFLUENCE (link).
- Networking module v2 with explicit inputs/outputs (subnet map, route table ids, nat allocations) published and versioned.
- Automated state rewrite scripts (terraform state mv + provider meta) available in repo and tested on a dev workspace.
- CI pipeline gates: terraform fmt/validate/plan with provider lockfile and terratest smoke runs.
- Canary migration completed for infra-dev-1 and infra-staging-2 with monitored perf & drift for 48h.
- Rollback steps documented and verified.
- PRs merged and release tag infra-2025.03 created.
technical_notes:
- Provider-compat layer approach: create module infra/provider_compat that conditionally injects alias providers and maps deprecated resource names to new provider behaviors via wrapper modules (no runtime proxy). Use provider_installation block and explicit required_providers in root modules.
- Target terraform >= 1.5.0 and AWS provider 5.x (with ability to pin back to 4.x via compat variables during rollout).
- Networking v2 contract to expose minimal mutable state: public_subnets, private_subnets, route_table_ids, nat_gateway_ids, az_map. Avoid implicit EIP allocation inside higher-level modules.
- State migration: use terraform state mv to move resources from old modules to new module addresses, and provider meta adjustments when moving between provider versions. Provide safety checks to prevent double-creation.
- CI/QA: add a new github actions workflow infra/terraform-checks.yml that runs plan-only with provider lockfile, and a terratest job that runs basic apply/destroy in isolated dev account.
- Observability: instrument canary migration with cloudwatch dashboards and a short-term anomaly alert for increased NAT costs or route instability.
migration_plan:
1) Create provider_compat module and networking_v2 module in infra/modules (branch feature/eng-34277).
2) Add provider lockfile and update root module required_providers to support a provider matrix variable (aws_version_override).
3) Add terraform-checks CI and terratest harness.
4) Run unit smoke tests and a dry-run plan against infra-dev-1.
5) Execute state migration script on infra-dev-1, observe for 24-48h.
6) If stable, repeat for infra-staging-2.
7) Roll out to production workspaces in small groups with post-migration monitoring.
8) Remove compat toggles after all workspaces on target provider versions and mark modules v2 stable.
rollback_plan:
- If plan shows drift or resources would be recreated, abort and revert branch.
- If post-migration issues detected: run state-mv to revert resources to original addresses and re-apply old module versions.
- Maintain provider lockfile snapshot for quick restore of previous provider versions.
- Emergency contact: infra-oncall@redwood.com and paging list pager-duty infra-team.
testing_and_validation:
- Terratest cases: (a) networking_v2 creates and destroys subnets/route tables without orphaning EIPs, (b) state migration script moves at least 10 resources and state remains consistent, (c) provider_compat variables behave as expected toggling provider versions.
- CI checks: fmt/validate/plan must pass for all affected workspaces.
- Canary monitoring: compare ASG scaling, NAT bandwidth, and per-token latency impact for 48h after migration.
- Post-mortem checklist if rollback required and lessons learned captured in CONFLUENCE.
